title: Audit provenance enrichment and compact-delta format for RBAC v2
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Define an extendable audit event envelope and a compact delta micro-format that preserves identity provenance, SSO/SAML assertion context, and per-field visibility masks for RBAC v2 administrative actions. Goal is to make admin changes (role binds, policy edits, service principal rotations, SSO config updates) queryable, debuggable, and privacy-aware across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments.

Scope: 1) canonical envelope fields (event_id, ts, source, tenant_id, route, severity, op_type). 2) actor provenance chain: primary_identity, assertion_hash(SSO), actor_type(user|service|automation|delegated), session_id, impersonation_chain. 3) target/resource descriptors with stable resource_id and resource_schema. 4) Compact delta format: list of change tuples in micro-format [op, json_pointer, compact_value] where op ∈ {add, remove, replace, redact} and compact_value is a deterministic encoding (base64 for blobs). 5) Visibility masks and redaction hints: per-field visibility {public, support, admin, pii} and redaction rules tied to tenant policy. 6) Sampling & retention hints: sampling_key and retention_tier to support high-volume systems.

Deliverables: schema spec, example event corpus for common admin flows, test harness for delta encoding/decoding, telemetry queries for Console, migration plan for existing audit streams.
acceptance_criteria: Schema document (JSON Schema + prose) published in docs: /confluence/rbac-v2-audit-provenance
Delta micro-format implementation library in runtime and audit-processor + unit tests
Per-field visibility masks enforced in Console (support vs admin vs public) in a feature flag
SSO/SAML assertion hash stored alongside actor_provenance without leaking raw assertions
Migration path: dual-write for 4 weeks with forwards/backwards-compatible decoder
Performance: event size overhead < 25% for common RBAC ops; decoding cost < 2ms per event in processor
notes: Trade-off: keeping assertion_hash instead of full assertion avoids PII but requires deterministic hashing with tenant-specific salts to avoid cross-tenant correlation
Decided to use json-pointer style paths for delta micro-format because they are compact and easily indexable
Compression: for very large policy blobs we will encode compact_value as zlib(base64) and mark op as 'replace+bulk'
Visibility masks are enforced at read-time by the audit-processor; consider adding encryption-by-key for admin-tier fields in Private deployments
Sampling: use stable sampling_key = sha256(tenant_id + route + actor_id) to allow consistent sampling across retries
